pressReleaseTitle: India Rating Revises Outlook on B.G. Shirke Construction’s Bank Loans to Positive; Affirms ‘IND A+
issuerName: B.G. Shirke Construction Technology Pvt. Ltd.
overview: India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) has revised the Outlook on B.G. Shirke Construction Technology Pvt. Ltd’s (BGSCTPL) bank loan ratings to Positive from Stable while affirming the ratings as follows:
overviewHTML: Ind-Ra continues to consider BGSCPTL’s standalone financials to arrive at the ratings while factoring in the debt guaranteed for its wholly owned subsidiary B G Shirke Redevelopment and Gas Pvt. Ltd. (BGSRGPL) till FY23, which was repaid in FY24.
keyRatingDrivers:
Continued Strong Operating Performance:  BGSCPTL’s operating performance remained strong as reflected by its revenue increasing at a CAGR of 11% over FY20-FY24, due to the strong execution of its order book. In 1HFY25, the company generated a revenue of INR27 billion (1HFY24: INR28 billion, FY24: INR58.9 billion, FY23: INR57.9 billion) and an EBITDA of INR6.5 billion in with 24% EBITDA margin (1HFY24: INR5.8 billion, 21% EBITDA margin, FY24: INR13 billion,22.1% EBITDA margin, FY23: INR12.5 billion,21.6% EBITDA margin), due to the strong execution of its order book. According to the management, the company’s strong profitability is aided by the bidding strategy as well as its in-house precast facility at locations near major projects which helps reduce the execution time and costs. BGSCTPL’s order book, including price escalations from construction contracts, which is the main line of business, stood at INR166.1 billion at end-October 2024 (end-July 2023: INR104.9 billion, May 2022: INR124.15 billion), providing an orderbook visibility of about 2.8x of its FY24 revenues. In the large order book, INR45 billion of the orders were received in FY25 and are likely to contribute 4QFY25/1QFY26 onwards.


Robust Credit Metrics: BGSCTPL's credit metrics were robust in FY24 owing to a rise in the EBITDA and a decline in the interest costs. The net adjusted leverage (including acceptances and outstanding against CG given) was 0.01x at end-1HFY25 (FY24: net cash positive, FY23: 0.5x) and the gross interest coverage (operating EBITDAR/gross interest expense) increased substantially to 20x (11x, 9.1x). Ind-Ra expects the credit metrices to remain robust over the medium term, supported by the projected operating performance and the working capital cycle.  The total outside liability (TOL)/EBITDA also remained comfortable at 2.2x in 1HFY25 (FY24: 1.9x, FY23:  2.5x), backed by healthy cash flows.

Healthy Free Cash Flows: BGSCTPL’s cash flow from operations (company-reported figures) increased to INR11.6 billion in FY24 (FY23: INR9.5 billion, FY22: INR2.5 billion), driven by the increase in its revenue base and EBITDA. The gross working capital to revenues increased to 36% in FY24 (FY23: 31%, FY22: 36%), and the net working capital to 17% of the revenue (14%, 8%). The current liabilities have remained low over the past two years (FY24: 19%, FY23: 18%, FY22: 28%) due to a decline in the mobilisation advances, since most authorities have started charging interest on mobilisation advances, making them less commercially attractive; only Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority’s (MHADA) and City and Industrial Development Corporation’s (CIDCO) mobilisation advances do not entail an interest pay-out.  Ind-Ra expects the working capital cycle to remain at FY24 levels over the medium term since the company is largely operating with a similar mix of counterparties. BGSCTPL incurred capex of INR1.8 billion in FY24, and expects to incur incremental capex of INR1-billion-1.5 billion each year over the near term, which is likely to be funded in a mix of internal accruals and debt.

Exposure to Group Entities:  BGSCTPL’s gross loans and advances to its group companies declined to INR 2.3 billion in 1HFY25 (FY24: INR2.7 billion, FY23: INR3.6 billion), while its net loans reduced to INR 2.1 billion (INR2.5 billion, INR3.4 billion), including write-offs of INR0.19 billion (INR0.18 billion).

 

BGSRGPL, Shirke Recreation Enterprise, and Shirke Club Management LLP together accounted for about 91% of the total loans and advances provided by BGSCTPL in FY24. Till FY23, BGSRGPL had an outstanding gas division debt of INR3.4 billion (total debt of INR4.0 billion), for which BGSCTPL had kept in lien an equivalent amount of fixed deposit along with letter of comfort/undertaking; however, the same was repaid by the company during FY24 by liquidating the fixed deposits and the gas division of BGSRGPL has been reverse merged into BGSCTPL.

 

Ind-Ra does not expect any material fund outflows to support any other group company operations in the near-to-medium term; the same is a rating monitorable.

Concentrated Order Book: BGSCTPL’s construction contracts order book including price escalation, stood at INR166.1 billion at end-October 2024 (end-July 2023: INR104.9 billion, May 2022: INR124.15 billion). Geographically, BGSCTPL’s 83% order book is concentrated in Maharashtra, followed by 7% each in Delhi and Karnataka and the balance in Tamil Nadu and Madhya Pradesh.  Also 73% of the order book is concentrated in Maharashtra State Government bodies like MAHADA (39%), CIDCO (22%), Pune Development Region Development Authority (6%) and Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (3%). Of the total order book, 41% worth INR67.8 billion consist of projects where the work is yet to start. Although the company has a long track record of operating in this segment /geography of urban/low-cost housing providing it both competitive advantage and a strong association with the respective authorities; however, the timely start and completion of projects will remain key monitorable.
ratingSensitivities:
Positive: Events that could, individually or collectively, lead to a positive rating action are:

-   a continued improvement in the governance structure, including the availability of high-quality financial and operational data, while maintaining a robust credit profile with the net adjusted leverage (including the outstanding corporate guarantees and acceptances) remaining below 0.75x and/or the TOL /EBITDA remaining below 3.5x on a sustained basis

-   sustaining the current scale of profitability while maintaining or improving the diversification in terms of segments, geographies and counterparties

 

Negative: Events that could, individually or collectively, lead to a negative rating action are:

-   a decline in the profitability and/or an elongation of the working capital cycle

-   any material fund outflows to any group companies/ promoter payouts, leading to deterioration in the liquidity

-   the net adjusted leverage exceeding 0.75x and/or the TOL/EBITDA exceeding 3.5x on a sustained basis
companyProfile: Incorporated in 1994 (established business in 1944), BGSCTPL is the flagship company of the Pune-based Shirke Group. BGSCTPL is primarily engaged in the construction of housing projects for government agencies such as DDA, MHADA, CIDCO and Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana.

descriptionAboutIndiaRating:
India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) is India's SEBI registered credit rating agency committed to providing India's credit markets accurate, timely, and prospective credit opinions. Built on a foundation of independent thinking, rigorous analytics, and an open and balanced approach towards credit research, Ind-Ra has grown rapidly during the past decade, gaining significant market presence in India's fixed income market.

Ind-Ra currently maintains coverage of corporate issuers, financial institutions (including banks and insurance companies), finance companies, urban local bodies, and structured finance and project finance companies.

Headquartered in Mumbai, Ind-Ra has seven branch offices located in Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Gurugram, Hyderabad, Kolkata, and Pune. Ind-Ra is recognised by the Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India.

Ind-Ra is a 100% owned subsidiary of the Fitch Group.

detailedRationaleOfRatingAction: The Positive Outlook reflects BGSCPTL’s sustained scale of operations and profitability along with improvement in the credit metrics over FY24-1HFY25. Furthermore, with the high cash balance/adequate liquidity, coupled with the broadly stable working capital cycle, the company is positioned to scale up its operations over the medium term.
listOfKeyRatingDrivers:
Strengths

  • Continued strong operating performance
  • Robust credit metrics
  • Healthy free cash flows

Weaknesses

  • Exposure to group entities
  • Concentrated order book
liquidity: Adequate: Over the 12 months ended September 2024, the average utilisation of the company’s fund-based working capital limits was 32%, and the utilisation of its non-fund-based limits was 58%. The company’s fund-based and non-fund-based limits are largely from public sector banks. The on-balance sheet debt of INR10.7 billion at 1HFY25 (FY24: INR7.03 billion) comprised terms loan amounting to INR1.7 billion (INR2.2 billion), working capital debt of INR4.9 billion (INR3.5 billion) and inter-corporate deposits from related parties worth INR3.8 billion (INR1.01 billion). BGSCTPL had unencumbered cash and cash equivalents including mutual funds of INR10.4 billion at end-1HFY25 (FYE24: INR10.8 billion), against scheduled repayments of INR1.3 billion and INR0.4 billion in FY25 and FY26, respectively, which are likely to be repaid from internal accruals. The agency believes the low utilisation of fund-based limits and substantial cash balance provide strong balance sheet flexibility.
